newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ivory Coast will not disclose daily cocoa data.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast will not disclose daily cocoa data.

text.p: Ivory Coast is discussing the future of its disputed export auction system for cocoa but is not willing to give in to a request by international donors for daily trade data which it regards as confidential, Agriculture Minister Lambert Kouassi Konan said on Wednesday.
"We have refused to communicate the results of our day to day sales," Kouassi told reporters, commenting on recent cocoa talks with the World Bank, International Monetary Fund and other agencies.
Kouassi was speaking in Paris where he was attending a French farm show.

Cocoa and coffee sector liberalisation linked to a $150 million World Bank Agricultural Sector Adjustment loan led to the introduction in May 1996 of an electronic export auction system that the industry believes encourages overbidding for contracts.
Exporters want changes to the rules, complaining that some cannot get export contracts to ship cocoa through the system.
The World Bank has said it will not make a decision on any changes to the donor-backed system, which was introduced to increase dealing transparency until it receives data on daily cocoa trading.
Kouassi said that the detailed data was commercially confidential.

Changes to the system were part of the agenda for three days of talks in early February between Ivory Coast's government and the donors, the International Cocoa Organisation, the European Union, a French development agency and international cocoa traders.
The government has given few details of the private talks but officials have said it plans to discuss further reform of its cocoa industry in May.
